figures.intent: Convey MMRL++ architecture: dual frozen encoders, shared-residual aligners injecting tokens, PRC inter-layer composition, weighted fusion at output
figures.narrative: Frozen CLIP image and text encoders (gray) receive learnable representation tokens via the Shared-Residual Representation Aligner (SRRA, orange). Tokens are progressively composed across layers 6-12 via PRC (beta-weighted). The Weighted Fusion combines original CLIP logits and representation-enhanced logits at the output.

figures.intent: Show MMRL++ on the Pareto frontier of trainable params vs H-mean
figures.narrative: X-axis: trainable parameters (M, log scale). Y-axis: harmonic mean (%). MMRL++ dominates the upper-left region.

figures.intent: Effect of SRRA rank on H-mean and trainable params
figures.narrative: Rank r in {1,2,4,8,16} on x; H-mean (left axis), params (right axis). r=4 is the sweet spot.

figures.intent: Effect of PRC composition weight beta on base, novel, H-mean
figures.narrative: Beta in {0.1,..,0.9} on x; three curves (base, novel, H-mean). beta=0.9 maximizes H-mean.

figures.intent: Show that SRRA's shared base produces uniform gradient flow across layers
figures.narrative: Layer index (6-12) on x; gradient L2 norm on y. MMRL slopes up; MMRL++ is flat.
